reasoning: Recent information is almost entirely about the 2026 West Virginia Senate race; there is no fresh, state-specific presidential polling in the last 45 days in the gathered results. Prediction-market and forecasting coverage consistently indicate a massive Republican advantage, with Kalshi and Octagon describing Shelley Moore Capito as having roughly a 97% chance of winning and markets pricing a GOP margin well above 25 points. Structural data from Cook PVI (R+22) and similar sources, combined with these market-based expectations, point to the current West Virginia Senate race environment as roughly R+30 to R+35, with no evidence of any competitive Democratic polling surge in the last month and a half.

sources.name: OddsShopper (Kalshi WV Senate winner and margin markets)
sources.details: OddsShopper summarizes Kalshi’s West Virginia Senate winner market with Shelley Moore Capito (R) trading around 97–98 cents versus 1–3 cents for Democrat Rachel Fetty Anderson, and margin-of-victory markets heavily favor Republicans winning by 26+ points.

sources.name: Octagon WV Senate winner forecast
sources.details: Octagon’s West Virginia Senate winner page, using both its model and Kalshi prediction market, gives Shelley Moore Capito roughly 97% chances and describes her as a popular incumbent in a deeply Republican state, emphasizing an overwhelming GOP advantage.

sources.details: Polymarket’s West Virginia Senate margin-of-victory markets list the leading outcome as Republicans winning by 35–40 percentage points (24% probability), with 40–45% as the next most-likely band, indicating trader expectations of a very large GOP win.

sources.details: Polymarket’s separate turnout market for the West Virginia Senate election describes the contest as low-competition with incumbent Republican Shelley Moore Capito facing Democrat Rachel Fetty Anderson in a heavily Republican state, reinforcing the perception of a safe GOP seat though without a numeric margin.

sources.details: Decision Desk HQ’s collaborative forecast with The Hill for the West Virginia Senate race shows the Republican candidate with greater than 99% win probability and the Democrat with less than 1%, reflecting an effectively safe Republican seat without specifying an exact vote margin.
